title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_0RA---_1LA1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_0RA---_1LA1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, Collatz-like. Between resets the machine is a plain bouncer, and Lean proves that every reset starts from a tape 1 1 0 (10)y and runs ternary rounds (the middle block grows 2, 8, 26, 80, …). How a reset ends (rounds nested inside gaps of 0s) is read off runs, not proved. Resets from y = 1461, 3158 and 5834 halt (no other y < 3000); the orbit from blank tape (4, 38, 55, 144, …, 19656, 39352) avoids them as far as it has been followed.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,335 cells have been visited and 25,462 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.25). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.451).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Three one-sweep rules found and proved by bbtools.cycles, e.g. from (11)n+2 (10)m+1 with B at the right end the machine reaches the same tape with one 11 pair fewer and two more 10 pairs in 6m + 16 steps, for all n, m.

claims.title: Every reset starts from Q(2, y)
claims.text: With Q(x, y) = 1<sup>x</sup> 0 (10)<sup>y</sup> A>: the sweep Q(x+3, y) → Q(x+1, y+2), Q(1, y) → Q(2y+8, 0), hence every Q(x, y) with x ≥ 1 reaches Q(2, y') with an explicit y'; blank tape reaches Q(6, 0) and Q(2, 4).

claims.title: The ternary rounds
claims.text: Q(2, y+2) → C> 0 (10)2 1 1 0 (10)y+2 1, and one round C> 0 (10)a 1 1 0 (10)k+2a+1 R → C> 0 (10)3a+2 1 1 0 (10)k R for all a ≥ 2, k and tapes R; any number of rounds by induction. Leaf rules by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: The end of the rounds
claims.text: For every y ≥ 2 the reset from Q(2, y) reaches resetEnd y, an explicit Lean function: after the last full round L(a, K) with K < 2a + 1 the run either is back at the bouncer, Q(2a−1, 3) from L(a, 1), Q(p+1, m+2) from a round step S(p, m, 0), Q(2m+9, 0) from S(0, m, 1), or reaches a nested start N(P, M) = 1^P 0 (10)^M 1^4 0 A>, from L(a, 0) or S(p+2, m, 1). When the reset is over, reset_step gives the next reset Q(2, y′) (resetMap). From blank tape Lean follows the resets 4 and 38 and reaches the nested start N(35, 26) (blank_to_nested). Of the y from 2 to 3000, 1502 resets are over at once and 1497 nest; all three halting y (1461, 3158, 5834) nest.

claims.title: How a reset ends
claims.text: When a round runs out of pairs the leftover 1s become a gap of 0s and the same rounds start inside the gap, nested several levels deep; the reset ends at some Q(x', y'), irregular in y (4 → Q(15,2), 38 → Q(6,51), 55 → Q(17,53), …). Read off runs. The first step of this, from the end of the rounds to the nested start N(P, M), is now a theorem (see above); the nested rounds themselves are read off runs.

claims.title: Halting resets
claims.text: From Q(2, y) the machine halts for y = 1461 (2,574,053 steps), 3158 and 5834, and for no other y < 3000 (full runs of c/nq.c). The resets from blank tape are y = 4, 38, 55, 144, 396, 451, 1190, 3388, 4980, 5776, 6174, 19656, 39352, …

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: whether the reset orbit ever reaches a halting y. The end of the top-level rounds is a theorem, including when a reset is over; what is not in Lean is the nested phase that follows a nested start N(P, M), so the reset map is a theorem only on the resets that do not nest.

explainer.lede: Probably not, but nobody can prove it: a bouncer that rebuilds its tape at rare resets, and a few resets lead to a halt.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 39,335 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Every reset starts from 1 1 0 (10)<sup>y</sup> and runs rounds a → 3a+2, proved for all sizes.
The smallest reset that halts; then 3158 and 5834.
Every way the rounds of a reset run out, proved: back to the bouncer, or a nested start.

sections.heading: A bouncer trading 1s for 10s
html: Each time the head, in state A, reaches the blank cell right of the tape, the tape is 1x 0 (10)y. One sweep takes two 1s from the left block and makes two more 10 pairs: 1x+3 0 (10)y → 1x+1 0 (10)y+2. If one 1 is left at the end, the tape is rebuilt as 12y+8 0 and the sweeps start over; if two are left, a reset starts. Both are Lean theorems for all sizes (q_to_two), so every reset starts from 1 1 0 (10)y.

sections.heading: Resets
html: A reset from 1 1 0 (10)y runs ternary rounds at the left end: a block of a pairs 10 becomes a block of 3a+2 pairs (2, 8, 26, 80, 242, …), and each round eats 2a+1 pairs of the right block. Inside a round the head bounces between a shrinking block of 1s and the right block, moving pairs three at a time into the middle. This is proved in Lean for all sizes (round, rounds).

When a round runs out of right pairs, its leftover 1s turn into a gap of 0s, and the same kind of rounds start inside the gap, with the gap as their budget, sometimes nested several levels deep. That part is only read off runs. The reset ends with a new bouncer 1x' 0 (10)y', and x', y' depend on y irregularly:
For y = 1461, 3158 and 5834 (and no other y below 3000) the nested rounds end with the head in state E reading a 1 in the middle of the tape, and the machine halts.

sections.heading: How the rounds run out
html: A round needs 2a + 1 pairs on the right. When fewer are left, the round starts anyway and stops after some steps; there are five ways it can stop, and Lean proves each for all sizes:

L(a, 1)        ->  Q(2a-1, 3)            reset over
S(p, m, 0)     ->  Q(p+1, m+2)           reset over
S(0, m, 1)     ->  Q(2m+9, 0)            reset over
L(a, 0)        ->  N(2a-1, 2)            nested start
S(p+2, m, 1)   ->  N(p+1, m+4)           nested start

with N(P, M) = 1^P 0 (10)^M 1^4 0 A>: a tiny tank to the right of the pairs, whose own reset runs the rounds again with the pairs and 1s to its left as its budget. So the reset map is a Lean function on the resets that do not nest (about half of them: y = 4 goes to 38), and the open part is the nested phase. From blank tape the second reset already nests: y = 38 ends in N(35, 26).

sections.heading: What halting would require
html: The machine halts exactly if the orbit of resets from blank tape ever reaches a halting y. Those values are sparse (1461, 3158, 5834 below 6000), so a hit is unlikely, but unlike the related machine 1RB0LF_1LC1RA_0RE0RD_---1LE_1LF1RC_1LC1LA, where the halting values are 2j+1−2j−7 and the whole reduction is a Lean theorem, here even the reset map is not yet understood in closed form: the nested rounds are the next thing to prove.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.25). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.451).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,335 cells (292 left of the start, 30,020 right), with a density of 1s of 0.647.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer 1^x 0 (10)^y: each sweep turns two 1s into two 10 pairs; every reset starts from 1 1 0 (10)^y with ternary rounds (proved in Lean) that end in nested rounds; the resets from y = 1461, 3158, 5834 halt.
family: two-region bouncer with a Collatz-like reset
